correctness.rationale: The source theorem gives exactly two global cases. A periodic or recurrent interior point excludes the escaping case. A nontrivial periodic cycle also excludes local-uniform convergence to one interior fixed point, so it forces the uniformly quasiconformal homeomorphism, d-isometry, subsequential-identity branch. After that branch is excluded, the bounded case has one attracting or super-attracting fixed point and all iterates converge to it, which forces every periodic or recurrent point to equal it. The escaping case sends every orbit to the sphere, so no interior periodic, recurrent, or relatively compact orbit exists.

value.rationale: Periodic and recurrent points are central invariants in quasiregular dynamics, where globally defined maps can have abundant periodic orbits. The new Denjoy--Wolff theorem unexpectedly collapses this structure for non-elliptic ball self-maps: one recurrent point determines the attracting global regime, while a nontrivial cycle is a rigidity certificate for the isometric homeomorphism branch. This supplies a natural orbit-theoretic diagnostic of the source dichotomy without requiring explicit access to the adapted metric, and is therefore more than a cosmetic restatement.
